business_scope.primary_industry_name: Die-Struck Brass Cloisonné Polishing of Novelty Enamel Badges

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (single national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax differentiation applies to International Companies)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common-law heritage under the Constitution of the Independent State of Samoa 1962, Westminster-style statutes, and limited fa'asamoa customary-law recognition in land and Matai-title matters)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER-Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus), in force for Samoa since 13 December 2020 — operative FTA/trade-in-services framework covering goods, services and investment facilitation relevant to the enamel-pin merchandising model
New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards 1958 — Samoa acceded 12 July 1994; ensures cross-border award enforcement in Etsy/Stripe merchant disputes
Hague Apostille Convention 1961 — Samoa deposited accession on 12 April 2018; Convention in force for Samoa on 26 April 2019; governs authentication of the legalization bundle described below
OECD Global Forum / Asia-Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG) exchange-of-information framework — supports bank and payment-rail underwriting through Samoa's exchange-of-information arrangements

No comprehensive bilateral investment treaty or full double-taxation agreement is presently in force between Samoa and the United States, China, the EU, Australia or New Zealand; the International Company statutory exemption supplies the tax neutrality instead

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended), Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2007, International Companies Act 2009 (as amended, including beneficial-ownership disclosure obligations), Companies Act 2001 (domestic beneficial-ownership amendments), SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for licensed registered agents, and Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (SFIU) directives; supervised by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and the Central Bank of Samoa for AML/CFT reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT), Samoa; no further consular legalization required for Apostille-party destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Letter of Compliance) confirming the IC's active registry status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (MFAT) for bank and Etsy/Stripe merchant-underwriting verification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized bilingual Articles of Association (English / Chinese) reflecting the Chinese-name brand and authorized capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (MFAT); Samoan consular legalization in the destination state if that state is not party to the Apostille Convention; Chinese-language text accompanied by certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney executed by the ultimate beneficial owner appointing the SIFA-licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille in the residence jurisdiction, or consular legalization for non-Hague states, followed by registered-agent verification and SIFA record-keeping

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding screening of each shareholder, director and UBO against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK HMT sanctions and domestic Samoan designations via the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; PEP determination under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 for foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs and international-organization PEPs, with enhanced due diligence applied to any PEP match; negative-news and adverse-media review of the enamel-pin merchandising trading profile; screening results are documented in the registered agent's AML file and re-screened on a rolling 6-month cycle; any direct or indirect sanctions or embargo match, including embargoed payment corridors through Stripe or Etsy, constitutes a mandatory refusal or termination event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SIFA Registry maintained by the Samoa International Finance Authority — name-clearance and incorporation filings are submitted exclusively in electronic form through a SIFA-licensed registered agent; no direct-retail public portal exists; availability is checked against the Registrar of International Companies database under the International Companies Act 2009.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be expressed in Latin (Roman) characters for indexation; a Chinese-character trading name may be recorded as a secondary name or translation in the bilingual Articles of Association, with an official pinyin romanization noted for searchability; the statutory name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Corp', 'Incorporated' or 'Inc'; names implying a different entity type (e.g., 'Partnership') are refused; the name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing Samoan domestic or International Company.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Samoa (unless authorized as part of a brand name)
Finance or Financial Services (unless a relevant financial-services license is held)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal by SIFA, the registered agent may within 14 days file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of International Companies, annexing the SIFA availability checklist and any trademark or goodwill evidence; if reconsideration is refused, an administrative appeal lies to the Minister for Commerce, Industry, Labour and Trade within 30 days, with final judicial review available before the Supreme Court of Samoa; as a practical alternative, the agent may immediately re-reserve the same name with a distinguishing prefix or suffix, or adopt the approved Chinese trading-name variant while preserving the intended brand.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or address-only presence is permissible for this industry: the statutory registered office must be the physical office of the SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa (International Companies Act 2009), while die-struck enamel-pin manufacturing, polishing and fulfillment operations remain external to Samoa; Etsy and Stripe will require a separate merchant or return address, which may be a U.S. or other operational address, provided the Samoan IC maintains its registered agent, statutory records and annual agent appointments; no physical staff in Samoa is required for this low-risk merchandising scope.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: quantified annual on-site inspection probability of less than 5% for a Low_Risk_Standard non-licensed merchandising International Company; the realistic compliance event is a records-only examination of the registered agent's office by SIFA/SFIU or a targeted AML/CFT desk review; SIFA retains the statutory right of unannounced inspection through the registered agent, but no Samoan jurisdiction extends to the merchant's overseas fulfillment center.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; sections 5 (Incorporation), 7 (Memorandum and Articles), 18 (Registered Office), and 23 (Appointment of Directors and Secretary)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Form IC-1) together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors/Secretary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Samoa International Company; share capital may be denominated in any currency. No escrow account is required by law, but if a bank escrow is desired for creditor or counterparty comfort, funds may be lodged with a licensed Samoa offshore bank under normal custody arrangements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company adopt the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association presented to this Board and proceed with all filings required for incorporation under the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER that 100 ordinary shares subscribed by the founding shareholder be accepted and issued for the consideration stated in the application. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Samoa. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Board appoint [Name] as Director, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Principal Officer, each with authority to act within the Company's Memorandum and Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa (online or in-person window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request with two alternative names using Form IC-NR. The Registrar will search the International Companies Register and reserve an approved name for 30 days. The name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must not misrepresent the business as doing domestic operations.
required_dossiers: Signed name reservation request Form IC-NR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited terms, file a revised name request by letter within 5 business days; the Registrar will re-examine on a priority basis at no additional statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent or Samoa law firm; notarization by a Samoa Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, specifying the International Company's objects, share structure, registered agent clause, and governance provisions. Execute the document before a Notary Public in Samoa or a notary in the incorporator's jurisdiction with legalization by apostille if required. The registered agent must countersign the consent form.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized consent of first director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar identifies typographical or substantive deficiencies, submit amended pages with a cover letter explaining corrections; the resubmission is processed within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing with the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 (Incorporation Application), Notice of Registered Office (Form IC-RO), and Notice of Directors/Secretary (Form IC-DS). Pay the government filing fee of USD 150 by bank transfer or cashier's order. Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registered agent receives a query letter; the agent must respond with the requested clarifications or corrected forms within 14 days to avoid abandonment. The Registrar will then issue the certificate within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Registered Agent Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Company Registered Agent (approval maintained with MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office address in Samoa using the licensed registered agent's premises. Execute the Standard Registered Agent Agreement, which covers legal address, mail forwarding, and annual government compliance reminders. Submit the signed agreement to the Registrar as part of the statutory records.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Proof of identity of ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered agent declines to accept for internal compliance reasons, select another licensed agent and file Form IC-RA within 7 days; no additional registry fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Ministry of Revenue (for registration); Registrar of International Companies (for annual compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting to approve share issuance, officers, and banking resolutions. Submit the International Company annual return (Form IC-AR) confirmation and, if any physical activities are contemplated, register for a Samoa business license with the Planning and Urban Management Agency. For offshore tax-exempt status, no corporate income tax registration is required, but annual government fees are paid to the Registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Revenue or Registrar issues a late filing notice, submit the return with a covering explanation and pay any prescribed late penalty. A waiver may be requested for first-time administrative delays.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Business Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Samoa General Business License (required only if the International Company conducts physical domestic manufacturing, which is not permitted for offshore International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environment Protection Agency (SEPA) under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Registration required only for any pilot-scale enamel pin polishing workshop located in Samoa; if activities remain overseas, EIA registration is Exempt.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For any Samoa-based physical operation: wastewater pH 6.0–9.0, total suspended solids < 50 mg/L, oil and grease < 15 mg/L; airborne particulate matter < 100 µg/m³; solvent and VOC emissions must be captured with carbon filters where enamel curing ovens produce organic vapors; hazardous waste (acids, heavy metal sludges) must be manifested to a licensed waste carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) is mandatory before start of any physical workshop operation; structural load clearance for kilns and polishing equipment is required from the Lands, Survey and Environment Division; occupational workplace clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act requires a provisional risk assessment and display of a compliance certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Apia; online filing portal: SRA e-Tax / Samoa Tax Online Services (STOS) at https://www.revenue.gov.ws. International company registration is administered separately by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Samoa International Company (IC): (1) obtain Certificate of Incorporation from the Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 2012, including registered agent and registered office in Samoa; (2) apply to SRA for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) using Form IRD-001 accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, registered agent consent, and director/shareholder due diligence documents; (3) SRA issues the TIN and places the IC on the taxpayer register. The TIN is used for bank account opening and customs/VAT administrative dealings. The IC's international business income remains statutorily exempt from Samoa income tax and stamp duty by virtue of Section 220 of the International Companies Act 2012.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: A Samoa International Company is treated as a non-resident exempt entity for Samoa tax purposes. It is entitled to a permanent exemption from Samoa income tax, capital gains tax, withholding tax, and stamp duty with respect to all property, business, operations, and transactions conducted internationally. Income is taxed at 0%. Any domestic-source business activity conducted within Samoa is outside the statutory exemption and would be prohibited without a special licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not operate a check-the-box regime. IC tax exemption is automatic upon incorporation as an International Company and does not require a fiscal election. Available elections include: (i) redomiciliation/election for a foreign company to continue as a Samoa IC under Part XVII of the International Companies Act 2012; (ii) election to convert an IC to a domestic company under the Companies Act 2012, which would subject it to normal Samoa income tax at the prevailing corporate rate; (iii) elections as to share capital structure, financial statements, and annual return filings under the IC Act. No hybrid mismatch elections exist in Samoa domestic law; hybrid arbitrage is addressed, where relevant, through general anti-avoidance rules and economic substance considerations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act 2008, as amended by the Value Added Tax Amendment Acts 2012, 2017, and 2020, administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT$100,000 (Samoa Tala) of taxable turnover in any consecutive 12-month period for goods or services supplied in Samoa. A person carrying on a taxable activity that meets or exceeds this threshold must register for VAT with SRA. An International Company carrying on exclusively offshore business is not required to register; however, if it makes taxable domestic supplies (e.g., local sales or local input purchases attracting VAT credits), it should register to comply with VAT obligations and to claim input tax credits on exported enamel-pin production inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API clearance mandate is currently in force. VAT-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices in the prescribed form (paper or PDF) containing the particulars required under Schedule 5 of the Value Added Tax Act 2008, retain them for audit, and file VAT returns and payments electronically via the SRA STOS portal on a monthly basis. SRA may require digital record-keeping but does not operate a continuous e-invoicing clearance system similar to Latin American models.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Samoa qualify for zero-rating under Section 15 of the Value Added Tax Act 2008 when the goods are physically removed from Samoa within the prescribed period (generally 60 days of supply) and supplied to a person outside Samoa under a genuine export transaction. Supplies of services to non-residents who are outside Samoa at the time of supply and where the services are used wholly outside Samoa are also zero-rated. A manufacturer of hard enamel lapel pins may claim 0% VAT on export sales and recover attributable input VAT on raw materials, die-struck labor, and cloisomé finishing services, subject to SRA substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged electronically with the Samoa Customs Service evidencing the outward shipment of the enamel pins
Commercially complete invoice and packing list describing the merchandise, ISIC/HS classification, quantities, and export value
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill showing the consignor (Samoa IC) and consignee outside Samoa, with proof of physical exportation
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 credit advice demonstrating receipt of payment from the foreign buyer in convertible currency
SRA VAT export schedule and VAT refund claim form supported by source tax invoices for materials, processing, and freight services attributable to the export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict SRA audit scrutiny. A claim found to be fraudulent or unsupported triggers: (i) immediate assessment and clawback of the 15% VAT that should have been paid, computed on the full export value; (ii) statutory shortfall and evasion penalties, which may reach up to 100% of the evaded VAT, plus late-payment interest at 2% per month; (iii) possible criminal prosecution under the Value Added Tax Act 2008 and Tax Administration Act 2012, with fines up to SAT$50,000 and imprisonment for responsible officers; and (iv) for an International Company, a review of its Section 220 tax-exempt status, potential revocation or forfeiture of the IC certificate, and recharacterization of offshore transactions under general anti-avoidance rules, causing loss of the 0% effective rate and exposure to full Samoa corporate income tax on deemed domestic-source income.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa operates a licensed exchange-control regime under the Exchange Control Act 1980 and the Foreign Exchange Regulations 1984, administered by the Central Bank of Samoa. The Samoan Tala (WST) is freely convertible for current international transactions, but capital-account remittances by resident persons are subject to CBS prior approval or authorized-dealer authorization. For the Samoa International Company (WS_IC), the core operations, export sales, and merchant settlement proceeds are non-resident transactions: the IC may lawfully maintain foreign-currency bank accounts, receive USD trade proceeds, and remit dividends abroad without WST conversion or CBS profit-remittance approval. If the IC were to incur domestic Samoan expenses in WST, the local bank would require a normal conversion entry and supporting invoice; no additional CBS approval is triggered for external, non-resident transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa does not impose any statutory mandatory conversion ratio or fixed surrender deadline for export receipts. Under standard CBS authorized-dealer practice, resident exporters are generally required to route proceeds through a licensed bank within 180 days of shipment and to retain supporting customs, transport, and invoicing documentation; the proceeds may then be held in the original foreign currency. A Samoa International Company is treated as an external entity for exchange-control purposes: its USD receipts from Etsy Direct Pay, Stripe-equivalent intermediaries, and direct wholesale buyers are not subject to any Samoan surrender requirement and can be retained, pooled, and disbursed in USD without converting into WST.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in USD with international clearing and SWIFT access
Operational Account in USD/WST with correspondent banking through the BSP Pacific network
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account for USD settlement and local expense payments
Operational Account in WST with limited USD facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low-Medium. Mainstream open-banking fintech and EMI providers such as Wise and Airwallex generally do not support Samoa-incorporated companies because of corporate address validation, FATF/AML-country risk, and onboarding policy restrictions. Payoneer may provide USD receiving accounts for marketplace settlement in certain Pacific jurisdictions, but it will require full UBO disclosure, the Samoa IC certificate, and a notarized director passport, and it is not a bank holding account. Stripe does not currently support Samoa as a merchant country; therefore the WS_IC cannot onboard Stripe directly. To use Etsy Direct Pay or USA-origin card rails, the practical non-prohibited structure is to use a USD bank account in a supported clearing jurisdiction, or a licensed payment facilitator under the IC's own name; otherwise the legal route is a USD account at ANZ Samoa or BSP Samoa with Payoneer as the intermediary settlement engine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Local Samoan licensed banks almost invariably require face-to-face due diligence with at least one director and each beneficial owner owning 10% or more, either in the Apia branch or through an approved introducing bank with a private banker. Pure remote account opening is rarely granted for a Samoa International Company due to jurisdiction risk and the absence of a substantive local operations office. If remote onboarding is offered to low-risk enamel-pin export companies, the bank will still require full video KYC identity verification, apostilled board resolutions, and original corporate registry documents couriered to the relationship manager. For fintech/EMI rails, no physical SaMoan appearance is required, but directors must successfully complete independent video-verification steps and provide documentary proof of the IC's commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company structure with nominee shareholder possibility: banking underwriting will flag opacity, lack of economic substance, and potential misuse of offshore corporate vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, current Certificate of Good Standing from the Samoa International Companies Registry, Register of Directors, Register of Members, Certificate of Incumbency, a current Beneficial Ownership Declaration naming the natural-person UBO with passport and proof of address, sworn declaration that no nominee arrangements are in use, a board resolution authorizing account opening, and a legal-opinion letter from Samoan counsel confirming the IC is not subject to domestic tax or exchange-control restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No material physical presence in Samoa; the business sources enamel-pin blanks from Chinese subcontractors and sells through Etsy/Stripe, which can be viewed as offshore internet activity without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A dated business plan setting out the design-and-branding function of the IC, purchase orders from Chinese manufacturers, existing supplier contracts for brass die-struck cloisonné polishing, sales contracts with Etsy/Stripe marketplace operations, inventory and logistics agreements, shipping and courier records (FedEx/DHL), trademark or branding registrations, and a letter from the Samoa Trust/IC service provider confirming registered office and director responsibilities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated payment-platform flows containing numerous small USD deposits, chargebacks, refunds, and platform fees are a red flag for unidentifiable third-party revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: All marketplace statements from Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe/payment facilitator, a ledger reconciling each settlement to a corresponding customer order, refund-policy documents, shipping notifications with tracking numbers, customs declaration forms for HS code 7326/3405/8306, and a committed transactional correspondence audit trail with order IDs, customer emails, and sales invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-tax jurisdiction account receiving USD from US-origin marketplace sales creates source-of-wealth and potential money-laundering suspicion despite the low-risk goods classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source-of-funds file including historical Chinese supplier bank statements, the UBO's personal wealth justification, financial statements for the IC showing the enamel-pin business gross margin, the original export contracts, full customs clearing documentation, and annual statement of no local tax liability from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue demonstrating the company's tax-exempt zone status.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Initial equity and shareholder loans should be lawfully injected through a licensed authorized dealer using SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's or counsel's bank in Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia, or the United States. Beneficiary name must match the Samoa International Company exactly; field 70 should state "EQUITY INJECTION / WS_IC CAPITALIZATION"; the remitting bank should classify the purpose as direct-investment equity capital (equivalent to BPM6 Direct Investment equity). Because the WS_IC is non-resident, no CBS prior approval is required for an offshore-to-offshore capital injection; the receiving Samoa bank will request a certified board resolution allotting shares, register of allotment, and a source-of-funds statement for each beneficial owner. The capital should be held in a USD-denominated account to avoid any WST conversion risk.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All outbound supplier payments for enamel-pin materials and subcontracted cloisonné polishing should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 direct-beneficiary transfers to the Chinese or Southeast Asian manufacturer, or, for larger production runs, through an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (SWIFT MT700). The clearing orchestration is a USD corridor: WS_IC's ANZ/BSP Samoa USD account is linked to a US correspondent bank, and each disbursement must be backed by purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or courier airway bill, and quality-inspection certificate to pass anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. Marketplace funds collected via Etsy Direct Pay and Stripe-equivalent processing should be batched once daily to the Samoa USD account using a licensed payment facilitator (or, if a supported jurisdiction is needed, a USD account opened where the payment facilitator is licensed); no customer funds should be routed through WST unless required for minor local operating expenses.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST onshore spot contracts executed through ANZ Bank (Samoa) Limited or Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited, available only for proven WST operating expenditures.

Short-dated USD/WST outright forward contracts up to six months, permitted only where the WS_IC holds a genuine underlying WST exposure and uses the hedge for actual settlement, not speculative trading.

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) on USD/WST, available through international banks for non-resident entities to hedge residual WST translation exposure; the Samoa IC has no access to Central Bank of Samoa swap lines.

Natural hedge strategy by denominating all export sales, Etsy settlements, supplier obligations, and bank balances in USD, thereby avoiding any need for cross-currency swaps; cross-currency swaps are generally not practically available or economically justified in Samoa.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Renewal and Licence Fee Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (filed via licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; renewal must be completed before the certificate expires for the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of 10% per month or part-month of arrears; administrative strike-off and dissolution can occur after 6 months of non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Office, Registered Agent, and Statutory Registers Location
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained on file at the registered office in Samoa; signed statement submitted via registered agent to the Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm may trigger a requirement to file a full extract of registers; repeated non-compliance leads to late-renewal penalties and potential strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act; audit is required only if the shareholders elect it or if the Registrar issues a specific direction
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed accounting framework for tax-exempt International Companies; if financial statements are voluntarily prepared, IFRS or US GAAP is commonly accepted; records must sufficiently explain transactions and financial position

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No statutory annual UBO filing is imposed on Samoa International Companies; however, the registered agent must continuously verify and record beneficial ownership under the AML/CFT framework and must update the UBO register within 14 days of any share transfer or ownership change; an annual internal KYC confirmation is required by the licensed agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$6,000 per year if voluntary audit is requested

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Samoa International Company is a statutory tax-exempt entity under the International Companies Act 1987: no Samoa income tax, capital gains tax, estate duty, or withholding tax on income derived outside Samoa. The effective tax rate for international sales of die-struck brass cloisonné enamel lapel pins is nil, provided no Samoa-source trading income is generated. A licensed IC is not subject to the standard resident corporate rate of 27%; however, any non-international local business activity would be taxable within Samoa, and the company should not hold a domestic carrying-on-business licence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return is required. The only recurring filing is the International Company Annual Renewal/Annual Return, submitted through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) digital registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the anniversary of incorporation; for calendar-year aligned renewals, the SIFA annual deadline is no later than 30 June for the preceding year, unless otherwise stated in the Registrar's renewal notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, incorporation number, incorporation date, and registered agent reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner must state the exact IC name and number from the certificate of incorporation; verify that the licensed Samoa resident agent is unchanged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa and the physical/hyperlink address of the resident agent or administration provider.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Samoan registered office of the licensed agent only; a non-resident company must never list a private foreign street address as its Samoa registered office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors, shareholders, secretary, and beneficial owner schedule, including nationality and residential jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all non-resident directors/UBOs with passport and proof of address details; non-resident ownership is authorised and no Samoan tax declaration of foreign income is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax-exempt status, statement that no business is carried on within Samoa, and confirmation of compliance with AML/economic substance requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident board should confirm that all sales, delivery and payment routing occur outside Samoa; if the pins are sold through Etsy/Stripe, the merchant account should be held by the IC but all supply-chain contracts and payments should show the foreign trade pattern.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual renewal attracts a monetary late fee, typically 10% of the annual government fee for each month or part of a month overdue, plus reinstatement costs if struck off. Continued default beyond the statutory period gives the Registrar power to strike the International Company off the register, cancel its tax exemption, and hold directors personally responsible for unpaid renewal fees and reinstatement disbursements.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders under the IC tax exemption. For a non-exempt ordinary resident Samoa company, the domestic dividend withholding tax on payments to non-residents is 15%, subject to DTA reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because IC dividends are exempt at source, no treaty withholding reduction is required for IC distributions. Where a non-exempt Samoan company pays royalties, interest, or dividends to a resident of a treaty state, the payee must obtain a certificate of tax residency from its home tax authority and submit a treaty-benefit claim form to the payer before payment; the payer retains the certificate and supporting statement for the statutory record-keeping period (minimum five years). Samoa's principal comprehensive DTAs are with Australia and New Zealand; for other jurisdictions, domestic law applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For International Company payers, the withholding tax on cross-border royalties and debt interest is 0% under the exemption. For ordinary resident Samoan payers, the statutory rate is 15%; under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand DTAs, the rate is generally reduced to 10% for interest and royalties when the beneficial owner is entitled to treaty protection. Payments made by an exempt IC to its non-resident intercompany lender or licensor should be supported by documented arm's-length contracts; absence of documentation is a red flag.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No monetary threshold in Samoa tala (WST) has been promulgated for International Companies because they are outside the income tax net. There is no mandatory Local File or Master File for an exempt IC. The relevant threshold is practical: where total annual worldwide related-party revenue from cross-border sales exceeds the scale at which foreign tax authorities require OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation, the IC should prepare a lightweight arm's-length analysis covering the purchase of enamel pin blanks, die-striking and cloisonné polish work, and sales commission paid to any related marketing entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies an OECD/EU-aligned economic substance doctrine to International Companies. The IC must demonstrate adequate physical presence, staff, management and expenditure in Samoa, or engage a licensed Samoa international service provider that performs those functions. A pure shell company with no substance and no business purpose is exposed to deregistration and information-exchange referrals. For the subject activity (hard enamel lapel pin manufacture and e-commerce distribution), the IC may satisfy substance through contracting with third-party original-equipment manufacturers outside Samoa, provided the IC retains substantive decision-making, invoicing, quality-assurance, and bank-account control; if these functions are merely delegated to the non-resident UBO, the substance doctrine is violated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa IC as a personal treasury for the non-resident owner while falsely declaring a zero tax status, or directing Etsy/Stripe sales into the IC solely to disguise foreign-source taxable income from the owner's home tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoa International Companies Act 1987 and the Tax Administration Act 2012, false declarations to the Registrar are punishable by monetary penalties, cancellation of the IC's certificate, and compulsory registration under Samoa tax law if the activity is found to produce Samoa-source income. The Tax Administration Act authorises assessment of evaded tax, interest, and penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In civil recovery, the corporate veil is pierced where the IC is a façade: directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, penalties, and third-party claims. A director may be subject to travel restrictions while an offshore integrity investigation is pending, and criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC from a foreign UBO's laptop with no physical premises, no Samoan resident agent engagement, no board minutes, and no bookkeeping; or placing intercompany contracts with the UBO's wholly owned supplier that confer no actual decision-making on the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike the IC off, requiring an application for restoration with a penalty. The Samoa International Finance Authority may revoke the IC's tax-exempt licence and report the entity through the exchange of information mechanism to foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly allow the company to be a shell are personally liable for restoration costs, government fees, and any Samoa taxes determined to be overdue; they also face disqualification from acting as directors of a licensed international entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Etsy/Stripe payments without obtaining or verifying the identity of the underlying supplier/beneficial owner, refusing customer due diligence, or effecting cash-equivalent transfers through third-party processors in a manner that obscures transaction value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Non-compliance with Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended, triggers administrative pecuniary penalties, suspension of the international company registration, and regulatory impact on the licensed international service provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who is knowingly involved in money laundering is personally subject to criminal fine and imprisonment; in serious cases, asset-freezing orders and travel bans are imposed, and the director's personal bank accounts may be reached.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Carrying On of Business in Samoa
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Installing a physical production workshop for enamel pins in Samoa, employing Samoan workers, or maintaining inventory within Samoa without obtaining the required local business licence and breaching the IC's offshore-only status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Companies Act permits revocation of the IC licence; the company becomes an ordinary resident Samoa company across the board and is assessed on its worldwide income at the standard corporate rate, plus late-payment interest and penalties for unlicensed trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unlicensed-business penalty and any unpaid corporate income tax to the extent the company is treated as a bare partnership or the directors acted outside the company's capacity; the directors may also be enjoined from doing business within Samoa until the licence is perfected.
